assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting the spherical aberration of the objective lens broke a limit that had held since Scherzer's 1936 theorem and brought routine sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy to materials, interfaces and catalysts. It is a clear invention that opened a door to what could not be seen before, and its effect on materials science is large and lasting. I declare my own field's closeness and so hold the evidence to a strict standard.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps are the hexapole and quadrupole-octupole corrector designs (Rose, Haider) and the first working corrected TEM (Haider, Rose, Urban and colleagues, 1998). The supplied names fit that record, but Ondrej Krivanek's corrected STEM work and Maximilian Haider's and Urban's roles need checking, and Krivanek is not among the credited names, which makes a three-person configuration contestable.
assessment.maturity: Corrected instruments are in routine use worldwide for more than twenty years, and results have been confirmed independently many times. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Krivanek's independent corrected-STEM contribution is outside the credited names, so credit is disputed in the wider record.
The split of credit between the corrector design and the first working instrument is unsettled.
Possible perception of conflict because of my own field; I rely on the historical record, not on instrument familiarity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and its realisation, followed by Ye's work taking lattice clocks to the 10^-18 level, gave the most precise measurements ever made. It opens tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy, and may enable a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated lattice trapping at the magic wavelength, which is the original invention. Ye's group made decisive advances in precision and in the Sr clock. Two names give a clean and fair configuration. Hall and Hänsch recognition in 2005 leaves frequency-comb credit outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs now operate lattice clocks at comparable accuracy, and clock comparisons confirm the claims. The prize would be timely, though the redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Recognition could be judged premature if the applied impact is expected to come mainly after the SI second redefinition.
Contributions by Ye and others to the Sr lattice clock may overlap with Katori's priority for the original idea.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical coherence tomography is a measurement invention with large benefit to humanity, because it is the standard of care in ophthalmology. It is original and clear, and it opens new access to tissue structure at micrometre resolution.
assessment.attribution: Huang, Swanson and Fujimoto produced the first in vitro OCT images in 1991 and the group led the early development. Independent work on low-coherence interferometry in the eye (Fercher and colleagues) predates or parallels it, and I would want that checked, as the supplied names omit it. Huang was a student and Swanson was at Lincoln Laboratory, so the allocation of credit among the three is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use spans decades, and many groups have confirmed and extended the method. The topic is mature, but its status as physics rather than biomedical engineering will be debated.
uncertainties: Whether the invention counts as physics for this Prize.
Priority relative to Fercher, Hitzenberger and others using low-coherence interferometry.
The correct number and choice of laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, and the HgTe experiment that confirmed it, created a new class of matter with robust edge transport. It is a major conceptual advance with consequences for spintronics and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical proposal. Molenkamp's group made the first experimental demonstration (2007) in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not credited. The record is split between theory and experiment, and the three-name configuration is plausible but leaves out BHZ and the 3D topological insulator work (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Fu).
assessment.maturity: The effect is verified by multiple groups and the field is established. The 2016 prize on topological phases partly overlaps and could weigh against timing.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors such as Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D topological insulator community.
Overlap with the 2016 topological phase prize.
Nobel-level credit for the experiment versus the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics achieved strong coupling between a superconducting qubit and a single microwave photon on a chip, and it became the architecture for superconducting quantum processors and readout. The effect on quantum technology is large and original.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the architecture in 2004 and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated it in the same year, so the theory and experiment split fits a prize configuration. Early superconducting qubit work by others (Devoret, Martinis, Clarke, Nakamura) overlaps and the 2025 prize recognised the macroscopic tunnelling basis.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups confirm and use the method; strong maturity. The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may reduce room for another prize soon.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits.
Credit among Yale, Sherbrooke and ETH people and prior ideas for cavity coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)F(x) in 2008 started a new family of unconventional superconductors with Tc above 50 K. It was an original experimental discovery that was quickly confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the first report, in a single paper, and it stimulated the field. Attribution to a single laureate is clear, though the earlier Hosono group result on LaFePO and the contributions of Chinese groups raising Tc quickly will be discussed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation was swift and thorough. The mechanism is still unresolved and applications are limited, so the impact on understanding and humanity is less clear than for others.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled.
Limited practical use so far.
Priority and credit for the rapid Tc increases by other groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later of the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is a new window and an original instrument-led discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and the collaboration and Karle was a central figure in building the detector. A large collaboration complicates credit, and the AMANDA precursor and the contributions of other IceCube leaders (such as Gaisser or the spokespeople) need review. The pair is plausible but not certain.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance, and source associations are growing but mostly tentative. The discovery is mature but source identification is incomplete.
uncertainties: Source identification is incomplete.
Collaboration credit and the role of AMANDA pioneers.
Whether to wait for firmer source associations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1992 discovery of 1992 QB1 showed that a population of icy bodies lies beyond Neptune and changed our understanding of the structure and formation of the Solar System. It is the original observation and it is clear.
assessment.attribution: Jewitt and Luu made the discovery together, so a two-person allocation is natural and also would honour a woman discoverer. Predictions by Edgeworth, Kuiper and Fernandez are theoretical antecedents, not competing discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Thousands of Kuiper Belt objects were found later, and the result is firmly established and independently confirmed. It is old enough to be mature, but its fit to Physics rather than astronomy and planetary science may be questioned.
uncertainties: Whether the Physics Prize would treat a Solar System survey discovery as physics.
Role of other survey teams, such as Kavelaars and Trujillo, who found additional objects soon after.
